title: DNA tetrahedron-mediated vascular targeted delivery of astragaloside IV enhances distraction osteogenesis via PI3K/AKT/FOXO pathway.
authors: Feng, Yisheng; Fu, Haojie; Zhu, Peiqi; Hong, Shebin; Shang, Yinyu; Chen, Yanchu; Wei, Hongpu; Wu, Hao; Huang, Xuanping; Jiang, Weidong; Wang, Xudong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究DNA四面体递送黄芪甲苷促进骨再生的纳米平台，虽涉及DNA纳米结构但非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅用分子动力学模拟辅助信号通路分析，与TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Bone regeneration during distraction osteogenesis (DO) remains limited by insufficient vascularization, which delays consolidation and compromises clinical outcomes. Here, we developed a vascular-targeted DNA nanoplatform (TDN@Ast-AptCD34) for the delivery of Astragaloside IV (Ast), a natural compound with pro-angiogenic and osteogenic properties. The nanoplatform integrated a DNA tetrahedron carrier with a vascular-targeting aptamer (AptCD34) and was further incorporated into a biocompatible mHA-PVA hydrogel for localized and sustained release. Physicochemical analyses confirmed its stable structure, efficient Ast encapsulation, and enhanced uptake by endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs). Functionally, TDN@Ast-AptCD34 significantly promoted EPC migration, tube formation, and paracrine-mediated osteogenesis of jaw bone mesenchymal stem cells (JBMSCs), thereby reinforcing angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling. Integrated network pharmacology, RNA sequencing, and molecular dynamics simulations identified PI3K/AKT/FOXO signaling as the central downstream axis. Mechanistically, TDN@Ast-AptCD34 activated PI3K/AKT signaling and relieved FOXO1-mediated repression of angiogenic genes, which was validated by rescue experiments under PI3K inhibition. In vivo, the hydrogel-delivered nanoplatform markedly enhanced early vascularization and robust bone regeneration in a mandibular DO model, whereas these effects were significantly attenuated upon PI3K inhibition by LY294002. Collectively, this study establishes TDN@Ast-AptCD34 as a multifunctional nanoplatform that couples angiogenesis with osteogenesis via PI3K/AKT/FOXO signaling, providing a promising strategy for vascularized bone regeneration in challenging clinical settings.
abstract_zh: 牵张成骨（distraction osteogenesis, DO）过程中的骨再生仍受限于血管化不足，这延缓了骨愈合并影响临床结局。在此，我们开发了一种血管靶向DNA纳米平台（TDN@Ast-AptCD34），用于递送具有促血管生成和成骨特性的天然化合物黄芪甲苷IV（Astragaloside IV, Ast）。该纳米平台将DNA四面体载体与血管靶向适配体（AptCD34）整合，并进一步掺入生物相容性mHA-PVA水凝胶中，以实现局部持续释放。理化分析确认了其结构稳定性、高效的Ast包载率以及内皮祖细胞（endothelial progenitor cells, EPCs）对其摄取增强。功能上，TDN@Ast-AptCD34显著促进了EPC迁移、管形成以及颌骨骨髓间充质干细胞（jaw bone mesenchymal stem cells, JBMSCs）的旁分泌介导成骨，从而强化了血管生成-成骨耦合。整合网络药理学、RNA测序和分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟，鉴定出PI3K/AKT/FOXO信号通路为核心下游轴。机制上，TDN@Ast-AptCD34激活了PI3K/AKT信号，并解除FOXO1对血管生成基因的抑制，这一机制通过PI3K抑制下的救援实验得到验证。在体内，水凝胶递送的纳米平台显著增强了下颌骨DO模型中的早期血管化和强健骨再生，而LY294002抑制PI3K后这些效应显著减弱。综上，本研究确立了TDN@Ast-AptCD34作为一种多功能纳米平台，通过PI3K/AKT/FOXO信号耦合血管生成与成骨，为临床挑战性环境中的血管化骨再生提供了有前景的策略。
